## For this week, I'm practicing using for loops and map functions on tide pool data by Jenn Fields.

### As always we need to start by loading in our libraries

```{r}
##### Load Libraries #####

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

## For Loop Section:

### The first step is reading in our data and listing the files in a directory

```{r}
##### Read in Data and List Files #####

TP_Path <- here("Week_13", "Data", "TP_data")

# List all files in that path matching a pattern (here, anything with .csv)
# You can use regex to be more specific about filenames
files <- dir(path = TP_Path, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)

files

```

### The second step is pre-allocating space for the loop

```{r}
##### Pre-allocate Space for Loop #####

TP_data <- tibble(filename = rep(NA, length(files)), 
                    mean_temp = rep(NA, length(files)), # Column for mean temp
                    mean_light = rep(NA, length(files))) # Colum for mean light intensity 

TP_data # rows = # of files
```

### The third step is creating the loop

```{r}
##### Creating the Loop #####

for (i in seq_along(files)) { # loop over each file i times
  
  raw_data <- read_csv(files[i]) 
  
  TP_data$filename[i] <- files[i] # Add file name to file name column
  TP_data$mean_temp[i] <- mean(raw_data$Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE) # Add this value to the mean temp column
  TP_data$mean_light[i] <- mean(raw_data$Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE) # Add this value to the mean light tensity column
   
}

TP_data
```

### The last step is creating plots using a for loop

```{r}
##### Create a Plot #####

file_names <- dir(path = TP_Path, pattern = ".csv") # Just the file names

for (i in seq_along(file_names)) {
  
  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(TP_Path, "/", file_names[i]))
  
  site_name <- str_remove(file_names[i], "\\.csv") # drop ".csv" for the title
  
  p <- raw_data |>
    mutate( # Adjust the Date.Time column to be properly formatted
      DateTime = mdy_hm(Date.Time)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = DateTime, y = Temp.C)) +
    geom_line(alpha = .75, color = "#56B4E9") + # Color Blind Friendly 
    labs(title = paste0("Time Series of Temperature (°C) from ", site_name), x = "Date", y = "Temperature (°C)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", vjust = -1),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", vjust = 2),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
    )
  
  ggsave(here("Week_13", "Outputs", paste0(site_name, " Temp.Plot.png")), # Ex: TP1 Temp.Plot.png
         plot = p, width = 6, height = 4)
}
```

## Now for the Map Function Method:

### The first step is to bring in the files using purrr

```{r}
##### Read in Data and List Files #####

TP_Path <- here("Week_13", "Data", "TP_Data")

files <- dir(path = TP_Path, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE) # saves the entire path

files
```

### The second step is creating the list and calculating the means

```{r}
##### Create List and Calculate Means #####

data <- files |>
  set_names() |> # names each list element with its file name
  map(read_csv) |> # a list of 3 dataframes
  list_rbind(names_to = "filename") |> # stack them; list names go in a "filename" column
  group_by(filename) |>
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(Temp.C, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_light = mean(Intensity.lux, na.rm = TRUE))

data

```

### The final step is creating a plot using purrr

```{r}
##### Create a Plot #####

file_names <- dir(path = TP_Path, pattern = ".csv") # just the file names

save_temp_plot <- function(file_name) {
  site_name <- str_remove(file_name, "\\.csv") # drop ".csv" for the title
  
  p <- read_csv(paste0(TP_Path, "/", file_name)) |>
    mutate(
      DateTime = mdy_hm(Date.Time)) |> # Adjust the Date.Time column to be properly formatted
    ggplot(aes(x = DateTime, y = Intensity.lux)) +
    geom_line(alpha = .75, color = "#D55E00") +
    labs(title = paste0("Time Series of Light Intensity (lux) from ", site_name), x = "Date", y = "Intensity (lux)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", vjust = -1),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", vjust = 2),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
    )
  
  
  ggsave(here("Week_13", "Outputs", paste0(site_name, " Intensity.Plot.png")),
         plot = p, width = 6, height = 4)
}

walk(file_names, save_temp_plot)
```

#### The outputs folder should have all the graphs!
